ready3_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: The Beijing Happy Valley amusement park's “Twin Heroes of Heaven and Earth” first sends the passenger cabin carrying more than ten people to a height of 76 m, then lets the passenger cabin fall freely; when it falls to 28 m above the ground, the braking system begins to start, and the passenger cabin makes uniformly decelerated motion, just stopping when reaching the ground. If a certain tourist holds in his hand a beverage bottle of mass 1 kg, taking g as 9.8 \mathrm{m/s^2}, when the passenger cabin falls to a height of 15 m above the ground, how much force must the hand use to hold up the beverage bottle?

If a certain tourist holds in his hand a beverage bottle of mass 1 kg, taking g as 9.8 \mathrm{m/s^2}, when the passenger cabin falls to a height of 15 m above the ground, how much force must the hand use to hold up the beverage bottle?
ready3_open_rewrite.final_cot: The image shows that this is a twin-tower vertical lifting/falling amusement facility, and the cabin moves along the vertical tower track; the image does not provide additional numerical values that can be used for calculation. The problem text gives: the cabin freely falls from rest at 76 m above the ground, starts braking and undergoes uniformly decelerated motion when it reaches 28 m above the ground, and just stops when it reaches the ground; the mass of the beverage bottle is m=1 kg, g=9.8 m/s^2, find the supporting force of the hand when it is 15 m above the ground. First find the speed when braking begins: the free-fall distance is 76-28=48 m, so v^2=2g×48=96g. The braking segment is from 28 m above the ground to the ground, the downward displacement is 28 m, and the final speed is 0. Taking downward as positive, there is 0=v^2+2a×28, therefore a=-v^2/56=-96g/56=-(12/7)g, indicating that in the braking segment the magnitude of the cabin's acceleration is (12/7)g, directed upward. 15 m above the ground is below 28 m, so it is still in the braking segment, and therefore the beverage bottle has an upward acceleration (12/7)g along with the cabin. For the forces on the beverage bottle: the supporting force N of the hand is upward, and gravity mg is downward. Taking upward as positive, N-mg=m(12/7)g, so N=mg(1+12/7)=mg×19/7. Substituting m=1 kg and g=9.8 m/s^2, N=9.8×19/7=26.6 N.
